title: A complete complex with shifted rank-one residue has a tensor inverse
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and a Noetherian scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-pc-scheme]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_n=(R/\pi^n)_X$, $n\geq1$, and $\widehat R_X=\varprojlim_n B_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the module derived categories and internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the ordinary ambient derived tensor over the ring sheaf [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Let $M\in D(\widehat R_X)$ be derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], and fix $m\in\mathbf Z$. Assume that $M_1=M\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}B_1$ is isomorphic to $\nu_X^*L[m]$, where $\nu_X$ is the etale/pro-etale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $L$ is an etale sheaf of $R/\pi$-modules etale locally isomorphic to the constant rank-one module $(R/\pi)_X$.

Then there is a locally free rank-one $\widehat R_X$-module sheaf $\mathcal L$, meaning pro-etale locally isomorphic to $\widehat R_X$, and an isomorphism $M\simeq\mathcal L[m]$ in $D(\widehat R_X)$. Every $\mathcal L\otimes_{\widehat R_X}B_n$ is of etale origin and etale locally constant with finite free rank-one values. Put $M^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}(M,\widehat R_X)$. Both $M$ and $M^\vee$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and the evaluation maps in both tensor orders give derived isomorphisms
$$M\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}M^\vee\simeq\widehat R_X,\qquad M^\vee\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}M\simeq\widehat R_X.$$
For every $n\geq1$, the cohomological and Tor intervals of the reductions of $M$ and $M^\vee$ can be taken to be $[-m,-m]$ and $[m,m]$, respectively, independent of $n$. The empty scheme is allowed. No trivialization of $\mathcal L$ is specified. The ordinary tensor products in these evaluation maps are derived complete. Their canonical comparisons to the quotient-tower completed tensor products [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] are isomorphisms, and through these comparisons the displayed maps also give the two inverse evaluations for the specified integral tensor product.

source.place: Lemma 6.6.8 (pp. 52-53): perfect local models from locally constant perfect residue; specialized to a shifted residue line, with the resulting line and its dual evaluation

proof.text: Write $B=\widehat R_X$ and $k=R/\pi$. The quotient/constant-coefficient completion comparison identifies $B/\pi^nB$ with $B_n$ and identifies quotient-tower completeness with local derived $(\pi)$-completeness. Apply the residue-lisse perfect lifting theorem with $A=R$, $J=(\pi)$, and $C=L[m]$. Its Noetherian and completeness hypotheses hold for the complete valuation ring of the finite extension $E$ and for the given Noetherian $X$. The residue complex has its only cohomology in degree $-m$, with rank-one finite free values; tensoring its local model $k[m]$ with any degree-zero module gives a complex in degree $-m$, so its Tor interval is $[-m,-m]$. We obtain a pro-etale cover $U_t$ and bounded finite-projective $R$-complexes $P_t$ with $M|_{U_t}\simeq B|_{U_t}\otimes_R P_t$.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2, Lemma 6.6.8; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 09C6 (lemma-connected-adic-lisse), completed-coefficient version

proof.text: Omit empty covering members. The residue calculation for a completed perfect model gives $(M|_{U_t})\otimes_B^L k\simeq\underline{P_t\otimes_R k}$. At any geometric point of the nonempty scheme $U_t$, the hypothesis on $L$ identifies its cohomology with $k$ in degree $-m$ and zero in all other degrees. Hence the scalar Betti numbers of $P_t\otimes_R^L k$ are $d_{-m}=1$, $d_i=0$ for $i\ne-m$. The bounded finite-projective representative makes $P_t$ pseudo-coherent (the equivalent projective-representative criterion in the cited finite-free-model lemma). Apply the local pseudo-coherent minimal-model theorem to the local ring $R$. Its representative has term $R^{d_i}$ in degree $i$; thus its only term is $R$ in degree $-m$, with zero differentials. Consequently $P_t\simeq R[m]$, and $M|_{U_t}\simeq B|_{U_t}[m]$.

Put $\mathcal L=\mathcal H^{-m}(M)$. Exactness of restriction (on underlying abelian sheaves, hence also on module sheaves) gives $\mathcal L|_{U_t}\cong B|_{U_t}$ and $\mathcal H^i(M)|_{U_t}=0$ for $i\ne-m$. A sheaf with zero restriction to a cover is zero, by the separatedness axiom, so these cohomology sheaves vanish globally. For a representative complex $K$ of $M$, the smart truncation $\tau_{\le -m}K\to K$ and the quotient $\tau_{\le -m}K\to\mathcal H^{-m}(K)[m]$ are quasi-isomorphisms: their cohomology maps are identities in degree $-m$ and all other cohomology is zero. This gives $M\simeq\mathcal L[m]$ in the derived category. It uses the global cohomology sheaf, and does not try to glue arbitrarily chosen derived trivializations.

source.place: Exact restriction to localized sites; smart truncation of a complex with one nonzero cohomology sheaf

proof.text: Set $\mathcal L^*=\mathcal Hom_B(\mathcal L,B)$. The line-evaluation inverse-pair theorem gives a line $\mathcal L^*$, both specified sheaf evaluations, and inverse exact tensor equivalences. By the sheaf tensor--Hom adjunction, $\mathcal Hom_B(\mathcal L,-)$ is the right adjoint of tensoring with $\mathcal L$, so is naturally the inverse equivalence $-\otimes_B\mathcal L^*$; it is therefore exact. Applying this exact functor to a K-injective resolution $B\to I$ is a quasi-isomorphism from $\mathcal L^*$ to $\mathcal Hom_B(\mathcal L,I)$. The defining Hom-complex formula, including its usual differential, shifts this result by $[-m]$ when its first input is $\mathcal L[m]$. It follows that $M^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_B(M,B)\simeq\mathcal L^*[-m]$. The unbounded derived line-tensor theorem computes tensor with either line termwise and is compatible with shifts. Hence the specified derived evaluations are isomorphisms in both orders: they are the derived images of the line evaluations with the cancelling shifts. On local bases their degree-zero evaluation is multiplication (with the standard Koszul shift/symmetry signs when the order is reversed).

source.place: Tags 0B8Q and 0B8N (line evaluations and inverse exact equivalences); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU (derived tensor)

proof.text: Both $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal L^*$ are flat, by the line-tensor theorem. Thus the derived reductions of $M$ and $M^\vee$ are respectively $\mathcal L_n[m]$ and $\mathcal L_n^*[-m]$, where $\mathcal L_n=\mathcal L\otimes_B B_n$ and $\mathcal L_n^*=\mathcal L^*\otimes_B B_n$. Restricting the same trivializing cover makes each of these sheaves equal to $B_n$. They are locally constant with finite stalks, since $R/\pi^n$ is a finite ring. The pro-etale/etale local-constancy equivalence therefore descends each to a finite locally constant etale module sheaf. On a nonempty etale trivializing member its constant value has geometric stalk isomorphic to $R/\pi^n$, so the value is itself free of rank one. This proves the asserted etale local rank-one property for every $n$, for the line and also for its dual.

The completed perfect-model lemma with the degree-zero complex $P=R$ makes $B[0]$ locally derived $(\pi)$-complete. The quotient/constant-coefficient comparison identifies this with quotient-tower completeness. Apply the integral line-tensor comparison with $C=B[0]$, first $T=\mathcal L$ and then $T=\mathcal L^*$. Its left side is $T$ and its right side is exactly $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(T\otimes_B B_n)$, through the canonical quotient maps. It follows that both lines are derived complete. Shifting this quotient-tower isomorphism by $m$ or $-m$ shows the same for $M$ and $M^\vee$; shifts commute with the products and cone defining this derived limit.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12(4), Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2; completed-line specialization

proof.text: For every $n$, each reduced line and its dual is flat and finite locally constant. The partition consisting of $X$ itself verifies finite-torsion constructibility. Tensoring $\mathcal L_n[m]$ with any degree-zero $B_n$-module sheaf gives its ordinary tensor with $\mathcal L_n$, shifted by $m$, and therefore has cohomology only in degree $-m$. For $\mathcal L_n^*[-m]$ the same calculation puts cohomology in degree $m$. Taking the other factor to be $B_n$ gives the cohomological intervals too. The intervals $[-m,-m]$ and $[m,m]$ are independent of $n$. Together with completeness from Step 6, these are exactly the defining conditions for both objects to belong to $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$. For the empty scheme all the sheaves and complexes are zero, the evaluations are isomorphisms, and the same intervals satisfy every vanishing condition.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1 and Lemmas 6.5.3--6.5.4; uniform shifted-line Tor calculation

proof.text: Finally apply ordinary/ completed tensor comparison to $(M,M^\vee)$ and $(M^\vee,M)$, which are now known to be bounded constructible derived-complete objects. A Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact, by its finite affine cover, and, being locally Noetherian, quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], as required. The theorem proves that both ordinary tensors are complete and that their canonical comparisons to the specified quotient-tower completed tensors are isomorphisms. Composing the two ordinary evaluations of Step 4 with the inverses of these comparisons gives the two inverse evaluations for the specified integral tensor product. This uses the canonical comparisons induced by coefficient quotient maps, so it identifies the tensor product stipulated in the item.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.5 and Definition 3.4.10; quotient-tower comparison of Lemma 3.4.12(4)

The lift lemma's hypotheses hold: O_E is Noetherian and complete; X is Noetherian with a finite affine cover; C = L[m] has f.g. locally constant cohomology; its Tor window is [−m,−m] because L is flat. Step 5: R/π^n is finite, so lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin(b) applies, and rank one is read off a stalk.
